children: announced investments in its physical infrastructure to improve service, adapt to changing network conditions, and create stronger connections for a more resilient network.

Using new artificial intelligence capabilities, the world’s second-largest telecom launched new AI-powered Autopilot that enables the network to make adjustments faster as conditions change, while an expanded Dynamic CX uses AI to anticipate demand and optimize performance.
The upgrades were built into T-Mobile’s
Self-Organizing Network (SON). If a cell site goes down, AutoPilot can quickly engage other sites to close coverage gaps, minimizing disruptions to customers. According to T-Mobile
, AutoPilot can make real-time network adjustments in about half the time.

“With AutoPilot, we’re taking the intelligence already built into our Self-Organizing Network and giving it even more ability to respond as conditions change, whether that means helping close a coverage gap caused by extreme weather, optimizing performance, or keeping customers connected during unexpected disruptions,” T-Mobile CTO John Saw said in a press release.

title: T-Mobile builds AI capabilities into network to limit disruptions, close coverage gaps
